paragraphs.text: Good evening, sisters and elders. It was great seeing all of your videos today. And Sister Hughes has been showing me some of the English language videos you've been sending to her. Very strong, very strong. It's exciting to see that growth and development in your skill, but also in your comfort being behind the camera, or I should say in front of the camera.

Today I was meeting with the assistants and they shared with me about how many lessons you taught last week to members, new people and total investigators. I was blown away, I'll be honest. I had no idea you were getting that much good done. You have really become effective working online. This is incredible. It's got me actually very excited about what the possibilities might be over the course of the next few weeks and what would happen as we came out of this quarantine.

It's going to be over. Some day, I mean whether it's in a week or two weeks or four weeks, one of these days it's going to end. And based on what you're doing, if you can continue to show consistency in delivering that kind of effort, well you're going to have an awful lot of people that will be ready to enter into the Covenant. And that's going to be pretty exciting. I mean the idea that we could potentially have a day, one day where we ended up having 100 souls entered into the waters of baptism mission-wide, I mean that's something.

Well the assistants will be talking to you more about those details as we get closer over the course of the next few days. But I think this could be big and it's because of what you're doing. It's because you're getting outside of your comfort zone and you're doing things that are creative but also inspiring. And you're bringing the spirit into people's homes and you're lifting them up and you're encouraging them. And as a result, God's pleased with you for sure. But you're also bringing joy to other people and people resonate with that. They want to have that feeling. They want to have that spirit. So anyway, exciting, exciting.

But the key is consistency. You're going to have to be consistent with this. We just can't have a great week and then fall right off the wagon. So I want to talk just a minute with you about consistency today.

You all know the story about the tortoise and the hare or sometimes called the turtle and the rabbit. The rabbit was fast but he was not consistent. The turtle was slow but he was very consistent and you know the end of the story. The turtle actually wins the race. And the great moral of the story, the great point of the story is that slow and steady is what really gets the reward in the end. You can be super fast, talented or some other attribute but if you're not consistent in using that attribute you're going to end up falling short most of the time and things that you're setting yourself up for a goal.

There's a great quote by one of the presidents of the United States by the name of Calvin Coolidge that I just love. It's been something that I've pondered and thought about for many, many years. It goes like this, quote, "nothing in the world can take the place of persistence." You could call that consistency as well. But persistence means that you are persisting to be consistent.

"Again, nothing in the world can take the place of persistence. Talent will not; nothing is more common than unsuccessful men with talent. Genius will not; unrewarded genius is almost a proverb. Education will not; the world is full of educated derelicts. Persistence and determination alone are omnipotent. The slogan 'press on' has solved and always will solve the problems of the human race."

Now let's just be honest with ourselves. There are so many people in the world that are so much more talented than you or me. They're smarter, richer, more creative, more likeable, more charming, better connected, better looking. But there is one singular thing you can do better than them if you want to. You can outwork them consistently. This commitment to just keep going no matter what always beats the stronger opponent every time.

Many of these super talented people have become successful without having to really bear down and be consistent. They never learned how to get that skill, that discipline. So if it doesn't come to them quickly, they just move on, try something else.

The famous actor Will Smith once was asked how he got to be so successful. And he said, quote, "the only thing that I can see that I have that's different is that I'm not afraid to die on the treadmill. I will not be outworked, period. You might have more talent than me. You might be smarter than me. You might be sexier than me. You might be all of those things more than me. But if we get on the treadmill together, there's two things: you're going to get off first or I'm going to die".

What Will Smith is teaching us there is that it doesn't matter how talented you are. It doesn't matter about all of the things. If you're a quitter, it isn't going to help you. And if you, on the other hand, are somebody that just isn't going to quit, you're just going to stay in there. You're going to stay in there until the other guy quits. You're going to stay in there until, as the scripture says, if you resist the devil, he'll flee from you.

And as you are focused on being consistently disciplined, consistently diligent, what happens is everything starts to come your way. All of the obstacles begin to drop by the wayside and the rewards start coming to you. And here's the beautiful thing. Anybody can build the discipline of consistent diligence. You can build this yourself in you. So you already built it, but all of us can build it. And here it is. It's the single most important thing you need to learn.

Because honestly, it's the one thing that separates us from the other people who may be smarter, better in so many different ways than us. If you're consistent, if you're focused in your diligence and you stick with it, what happens is you separate yourself from the herd. You separate yourself from the pack. If you can learn to cultivate that consistency in your work, you'll eventually beat anybody with more talent, anybody with more luck, anybody with more skill, just by being consistently and outworking them.
So my hope for you elders and sisters is that you'll choose to use these days of the lockdown to build the powerful habit of consistent diligence.

Good night. Let's enjoy conference tomorrow. And since you'll be getting so many inspiring messages during conference, I won't be sharing an update on Sunday. But I'm going to be sharing conference with you. So let's enjoy listening to prophets and apostles and other leaders of the church as they give us guidance that can bless us in the coming days. God bless all of you. Have a wonderful evening.
